titleEn: Down the Hill, Step by Step!

pages.text: "I will be first!" Lulu raced down from the hilltop. "Wait for us!" the cousins called, already far behind. Lulu wanted to reach the yard first.
On the steep slope, the feet went faster. Lulu wanted to stop, but the feet would not obey. "Ohhh!" Then a stone underfoot!
Lulu rolled into the grass beside the path. Dirt on knees and forepaws. "Ow..." Lulu sat rubbing a knee.
Uncle Beppo came slowly downhill with his walking stick. "Are you hurt?" He helped Lulu up. "I tried to stop, but my feet would not!"
He poked the path with his stick. "Downhill, go like this. Tap, tap, tap." Neat stick marks dotted the dirt.
"Step on one mark at a time." He led. Lulu stepped on one mark, then another. The feet did not speed up. "Down the hill, step by step!"
The cousins followed the marks in a line. Four sets of feet stepped steadily. Autumn leaves rustled underfoot.
At the yard, no scraped knees, no panting. "Slow, but not late at all!" Lulu hopped. Jingle!
Next day, Lulu walked down too. "One, walk, do not run! Two, one steady step at a time! Three, hold a grown-up's hand if slippery!" Uncle Beppo tapped his stick in the yard.
That evening, he stroked Lulu's head. "You came so well, without scraping your knees." Downhill, walk one step at a time. Lulu stamped one foot. "Down the hill, step by step!"
